topics.title: Router
topics.content:
Router is a layer 3 device that connects different networks. A router can calculate the best route for sending data from one point to another using an IP address.
 

Routing protocols: Routing protocols are sets of rules and procedures that routers use to communicate with each other to find and select the best paths for forwarding data packets across networks.

Routing Protocols & Easy Two-Sentence Descriptions
RIP (Routing Information Protocol)
RIP uses hop count to find the best path — like choosing roads based only on “fewest turns.”
It’s simple but old, and routers using RIP don’t know how fast or congested a link is.

OSPF (Open Shortest Path First)
OSPF builds a full map of the network using link-state information — like having Google Maps with traffic data.
It picks the best path based on cost (speed, bandwidth), making it fast and intelligent.

EIGRP (Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol)
EIGRP is Cisco’s smart hybrid protocol that picks routes using several metrics (delay, bandwidth, reliability).
It converges quickly, like a GPS that instantly recalculates if a road closes.

BGP (Border Gateway Protocol)
BGP runs the internet by letting ISPs exchange routes — like countries negotiating which roads connect their borders.
It chooses paths based on policies, not speed, making it extremely powerful but complex.

IS-IS (Intermediate System to Intermediate System)
IS-IS works similar to OSPF, using link-state logic, but is more scalable in very large networks.
Big telecom networks use it because it handles huge topologies with ease.

Static Routing (manual routes)
Static routes are manually added by the admin — like telling a router “always use this exact road.”
They’re simple and predictable but don’t adapt automatically if a link fails.

TCP/IP packet structure
topics.content:
In a computer network the data transfer happens in the form of packets. Packet mainly consist of three layers (IP header, TCP header, payload)

 

IP Headers: The IP header contains information needed to route the packet across networks, such as source and destination IP addresses. It ensures the packet is delivered to the correct device, even across multiple routers.


TCP Headers: The TCP header carries connection-related details like source Port , Destination Port, sequence numbers, acknowledgment numbers, and flags. It enables reliable, ordered, and error-checked communication between two devices.

 

Payload: The payload is the actual data being transported — such as HTTP content, API responses, or file data. It sits after the headers and is delivered to the application at the receiving end

topics.title: OSI model
topics.content:
OSI (Open system interconnection)model

 

  • It's a reference model that helps to understand how the data flows between client and server in a computer network.
  • The OSI model contains 7 layers and each layer contributes to specific activity to transfer the data from one network to another.

 

  • In OSI layers like application, presentation and session acts as software
  • Layers like network, data link, and physical works as a hardware component

The transport layer works as the heart ❤️ of the OSI model to connect and transfer data between one network to another. 

 

Application layer:  the interface between user and the computer. 
    Protocols: http, smtp, https.

 

Presentation layer: 

  • The presentation layer is also called the Translation layer.
  • The data from the application layer is extracted here and translated as required format to transmit over the network.
  • The data encryption, decryption, encoding and decoding takes place in the presentation layer.
    Protocols: TLS/SSL (Transport Layer Security / Secure Sockets Layer).JPEG, MPEG, GIF,

 

Session layer: 

  • It is responsible for establishment of connection, maintenance of sessions, authentication and security.

    Protocols used in the Session Layer are NetBIOS, PPTP.

     

Transport layer:

  • In the transport layer the data will be in segments.

  • It is responsible for ensuring the data is transmitted in the same order and no duplication of the data and it also ensures the error control and flow control of the data


    protocols used here are: TCP, UDP

 

Network layer: 

  • Here the data will be in the form of packets.
  • The network layer works for the transmission of data from one host to the other located in different networks.
  • This has devices like routers and firewalls.

    Protocols : IP, ARP

 

Data Link layer:

  • The data will be in the form of frames.
  • The data link layer is responsible for the node-to-node delivery of the message.

  • The main function of this layer is to make sure data transfer is error-free from one node to another, over the physical layer.

    Protocols: wi-fi, ethernet

     

Physical Layer:
It is responsible for the actual physical connection between the devices. 
The physical layer contains information in the form of bits. (Raw data)
Protocols: hub, bluetooth.

topics.title: How DNS Works?
topics.content:
1. When a computer needs to reach a domain say like (www.google.com)  it sends a request to a server called DNS resolver(DNS server). If the mapping for the domain is found in the DNS cache, the server returns the IP address. If not
  2. The resolver reaches out to the root server. The root server holds the indexes of top-level domains(TLD) ; there are 13 root servers globally.
  3. TLD names server gives the IP address of the authoritative name server (ANS), that holds the mapping for the requested domain name.

  4. If the authoritative name server has access to the requested record. It will return with Authoritative Nameserver info

    (ex: ns1.exampledns.com, ns2.exampledns.com ).

    This address info is returned to the client for the original request.

  5. The client now makes the request to the ip address and gets the response.

     

    An authoritative name server is a DNS server that holds the definitive, original information for a specific domain name, such as its IP address.

topics.title: Firewall
topics.content:
(A firewall acts as the first line of defense by blocking or permitting traffic based on rules)


A firewall is a network security system that monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic based on predetermined security rules. It acts as a barrier between a trusted internal network and an untrusted external network.
Firewalls can be implemented as hardware, software, or a combination of both, and they function by allowing legitimate traffic to pass through while blocking malicious or unwanted traffic.


Firewall Components and Validation
A firewall validates packet components such as IP headers and TCP headers in specific fields like source IP, destination IP, source port, and destination port.

 

Types of Traffic in Firewalls
Firewalls differentiate between two types of traffic: inbound traffic, which is initiated from the external network to the internal network, and outbound traffic, which is initiated from the internal network to the external network.


Firewall Actions
It acts like a security guard, filtering data packets to either:

Accept: Allow the traffic.
Reject / Deny: Block with an error response.
Drop: Block silently without response.

 

A firewall can take two main actions: block or drop. The "block" action prevents the packet from reaching its destination, while the "drop" action discards the packet without sending any feedback to the source. In contrast, the "deny" action prevents the packet from reaching its destination and sends feedback to the source.
 

IOCs in firewall: malicious ip address and Domain.

topics.title: Types of firewall
topics.content:
Network firewall: Network Firewalls are devices that are used to prevent private networks from unauthorized access. 

 

  1. Network Placement
    1. Packet filtering firewall
    2. Stateful inspection firewall
    3. Proxy firewall(application level gateway)
    4. circuit -level gateway
    5. Web Application Firewall (WAF)
    6. Next-Generation Firewall (NGFW)
    7. Network address translation (NAT) firewalls
    8. Cloud firewalls
    9. Unified threat management(UTM) firewalls
  2. System protected.
    1. Network firewall.
    2. Host-based firewall.
  3. Data filtering method.
    1. Perimeter firewall.
    2. Internal firewall.
    3. Distributed firewall.
  4. Form factors.
    1. Hardware firewall
    2. Software firewall

 

Packet filtering firewall : It checks packet headers—like IP address, port number, and protocol—and decides whether to allow or block them. Think of it like checking someone's ID at the gate. If the name and ID match the list, they’re allowed in, no questions asked. They are relatively simple and fast but might not offer the level of protection as more advanced firewalls.

 

 

Stateful inspection firewall: It monitors active connections and makes decisions based on the context of traffic. Imagine a hotel that remembers you checked in earlier, so it doesn’t question you every time you enter.

 

circuit -level gateway:  it monitors the connections between networks, ensuring they follow proper protocols. These firewalls provide better security than packet-filtering firewalls. But are still limited in their ability to inspect data payloads.

 

 

Network address translation (NAT) firewalls: it acts as a gatekeeper, allowing the devices to communicate with the internet while hiding their individual address, making it harder for outsiders to target them.

 

Proxy firewall(application level gateway): This acts like a middleman between user and destination. While hiding the internal address and filtering requests.

 

Web Application Firewall (WAF): Specifically protects websites and web apps from attacks like SQL injection or cross-site scripting. Imagine a form guard that checks what users type before it reaches your website—blocking any harmful tricks.

 

Next-Generation Firewall (NGFW): Combines traditional firewalls with modern features like app control, intrusion prevention, malware detection, and encrypted traffic inspection. It’s like a security team with surveillance cameras, ID scanners, and behavior monitoring—all working together. This is often found in large organisations to protect large amounts of data transfer.

 

 

Cloud firewalls: as the name says it provides security to cloud based networks and applications. They offer advantage of scalability and ease of management as they can be easily deployed and updated.

 

Unified threat management(UTM) firewalls: this firewall integrates multiple security functions(e.g. Firewall, antivirus, content filtering) into a single device. 

UTMs combine NGWS with antivirus software, VPN and intrusion detection to provide a comprehensive protection system.

UTMs are used in small to medium sized organisations.

 

Network firewall:  Protects a whole network by controlling the incoming and outgoing network traffic—usually placed at the entry/exit point between your internal systems and the internet.

 

 

Host-Based Firewall: Installed on individual devices like laptops, servers, or mobile phones. It protects only that one system.

 

 

Application layer firewall: inspects traffic at the application layer to block specific applications

topics.title: IPS IDS
topics.content:
IPS: intrusion prevention system

IDS: intrusion detection system

Both work on the principle of comparing the current network traffic and the known threat database then making the decision.

IPS: is an active system, typically placed inline with the firewall, that not only detects threats but also automatically blocks or prevents them in real-time.

IDS: s a passive monitor that analyzes traffic for threats and alerts administrators to take necessary action.

 

Conclusion: IPS acts as controlling system whereas IDS acts as more of monitoring system

Difference between IPS and IDS

IDS scans the traffic and detects malicious traffic and reports it to the admin based on network signature.

IPS scans the traffic, detects and can also block(prevent) the malicious traffic based on network signature.

topics.title: ESA

  • ESA is a dedicated security solution designed to safeguard the organization from phishing and spam emails.
  • The ESA verifies the sender and recipient details of email authenticators like SPF, DKIM, DMARC any URL and attachments associated with the emails.

  • DKIM: Domain key identifier mail. Which helps to identify the integrity of the email to make sure the email is not tampered by using cryptographic signatures (encryption, decryption or hashing). 
  • DMARC: Domain based message authentication reporting and conformance,  which is a combination of the both DKIM and SPF validated both authentication and authorization.
  • Threat intelligence report checks the file attachments and URLs
  • MX record:  its stores details of mails and IPs

 

IOCs in ESA: malicious file hashes, malicious URLs.

topics.title: What happens when you type in an URL in your browser?

When you type in www.google.com into address bar of the browser.

  1. The client needs to find the IP address of the url.
    1. Browser checks if the cache has the IP address for entered domain name.
    2. If there is no IP mapping. It will check the OS cache.
    3. If the OS cache does not have the IP address,  the client initiates a DNS request to the configured DNS server.
  2. Once the client has the IP address of the URL, the browser initiates a TCP connection with the server.
  3. The browser sends an http request to the webserver.
  4. The server handles the requests and sends back a response.
  5. The browser displays the HTML content.

topics.title: What is VPN?
topics.content:
A virtual private network(VPN) extends a private network across a public network, and enables users to send and receive data across public networks as if they were directly connected to the private network. it creates a secure encrypted tunnel between your device and the entire network.

There are two types of VPN: 

 

  1.  Site to site VPN. Connects two or more separate networks (e.g., main office and branch office) over the internet, creating a single, unified network.
  2. Remote VPN. Allows individual users (employees) to securely connect to a private network (like a company's) from anywhere, acting as if they're physically there.

topics.title: Difference between IPS and firewall
topics.content:
A firewall inspects TCP/IP header working on ACLs.

IPS does deep packet inspection (checks both header and payload) using network signature.

topics.title: Where do you place IPS?
topics.content:
An IPS is usually placed after the firewall. Firewall does the heavy lifting of blocking the unwanted traffic based on TCP/IP header. And of the traffic that is allowed, IPS will do deep packet inspection. Because of this IPS needs more processing power than a firewall.

If IPS is placed first, it will unnecessarily do deep packet inspection on all the traffic, while a good amount of traffic could have been blocked just by inspecting TCP/IP header with a packet filtering device like firewall.

topics.content:
CIA (confidentiality, integrity and availability)

  • Confidentiality: 
    • Confidentiality is  all about making sure only the authorized individuals can access the sensitive data.  Based on designation and roles.
    • Confidentiality can be achieved with the help of encryption and implementation of access control
  • Integrity: 
    • It is all about ensuring the data is not modified either in transit or in storage even if it is modified it has to be modified by the authorised users.
    • It's achieved with the help of hashing.
  • Availability: 
    • Availability is all about making sure the data or the information are readily available to all the authorized users
    • It is achieved by the help of a backup server and load balancers.

topics.content:

Risk :  potential consequence of the loss or damage of assets or data caused by a cyber threat.

 

Threat: is a malicious act that seeks to steal or damage data or discompose the digital network or system.

 

Exploit: the tool or mechanism used to take advantage of the vulnerability.

topics.content: Defense in Depth is a layered security approach where multiple controls are applied at different levels—physical, network, endpoint, application, data, access, and monitoring—so that if one layer is bypassed, other layers continue to protect the system.

topics.title: What is system hardening?
topics.content:
System Hardening means making a computer system as secure as possible by reducing vulnerabilities, removing unnecessary components, and tightening configurations.

System hardening includes:

  • Changing default user credentials.
  • Closing all unused ports.
  • Stopping all services that are unused.
  • Installing updates and patches.
  • Implement Access control.
  • Install antivirus and keep the signatures up-to-date.

topics.title: Zero trust model
topics.content:
Zero Trust is a security model that assumes no user or device is trusted by default and requires continuous authentication, least privilege access, and verification at every step.

Core Principles of Zero Trust

  1. Verify Explicitly - Always authenticate and authorize.
  2. Least Privilege Access - Give users minimum access they need — nothing more.
  3. Assume Breach - 
    1. Attackers may already be inside
    2. Systems can be compromised
    3. Logs must be monitored continuously

topics.title: What is the CYBER KILL Chain?
topics.content:
It is a step step process carried out by the attackers to conduct the cyber attack once they set the target. As a defender it is essential to understand the cyber kill chain, so that we can defend against the cyber attack at every possible step or phase.

created by Lockheed Martin, breaks a cyberattack into 7 stages — from planning to data theft.

Mnemonic to remember CKC:

R W D E I C A → “Rakesh Will Defend Every Inch of Cyberspace Always”

 

 

Reconnaissance: attackers gather the information about the target.

Gathering weakness of the target is goal of this phase

Weaponization: attacker builds or creates the weapon to exploit the weakness.

Ex: virus, malicious links, worm, malware

 

 

Delivery: selecting which way to deliver the exploit/weapon

Ex:- phishing email, usb ports, websites, attachments, qr codes

 

Drive by download.

Exploitation: it executes the attack code in the target sytem or once the payload is delivered the attacker exploits the vulnerability to execute the malicious code.

Goal: gain access.

 

 

Installation: it is the stage after exploitation where the attacker installs malware, so there access services, reboots, user logouts or attempts to remove the initial foot hold/access.

 

 

Command and control(CnC) 

  • Attacker gains the remote access
  • Attacker controls the targeted system remotely

 

Action on objects

Goal: Data transfer, ransomware, destruction

 

The attacker archives their primary goals

 

 

Exfiltration:  unauthorized movement of data. Or capturing the data without getting detected.

topics.title: About sony pictures attacks:
topics.content:
Date: November 24, 2014.

Attack: hackers gained access to sony pictures network and stole sensitive data including: unreleased films, confidential emails, employee social security, salary information numbers.

topics.title: About wannacry ransomware attack
topics.content:
Date: may 12 2017

Type: ransomware attack

Impact: infected over 200000 computers in 150+ countries, causing widespread disruption.

Method: exploited eternal blue vulnerability in windows SMB portal.

affected/impact: healthcare, finance, transportation. And other critical infrastructure.

The UK's national health service(NHS) was severely affected, other organizations, such as Fedex,deutsche bahn and renault also reported disruptions. 

Estimated damages were in billions of dollars

topics.title: Phishing attack
topics.content:
Phishing attack: it is a type of cyberattack where an attacker tricks a user into sharing sensitive information like passwords, OTPs, bank details or makes them click a malicious link or download malware.

 

Mitigation

  • Use email security solutions(to block obvious phishing and spam emails).
  • Educate users.
  • Use DMARC(Domain-based authentication, reporting and conformance).
  • DMARC is a standard for verifying the authenticity of an email. It offers email receivers a way to verify if a message is really from an authorized sender or not. 

Types Phishing attacks

Email phishing:

This is the most common phishing where attackers send mass fake emails pretending to be real companies.

Motivation is usually credential theft or malware delivery by making users click attachments or fake login pages.

Spear phishing

Spear phishing is a phishing targeted towards a specific individual, organization or business with customized research.

Whaling

This targets top executives like CEO, CFO, or directors using very personalized and urgent messaging.

Vishing

Here attackers call victims pretending to be support, bank staff, or government officers. Motivation is to extract confidential data directly by building trust and pressure in real-time.

Quishing = QR Code + Phishing.

Quishing is phishing through malicious QR codes instead of links or attachments. The attacker’s motivation is usually credential theft, payment fraud, or malware delivery when the user scans the code from email, posters, or chat.

topics.title: How will you detect phishing?
topics.content: By checking domain reputation, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, analyzing malicious URLs, verifying email headers, grammar inconsistencies, urgency pressure, and correlating logs in SIEM for abnormal access attempts.

topics.title: DOS and DDOS
topics.content:
DOS (denial of service) is a type of cyber attack where the attacker tries to make a network or machine unavailable for real users.

 

DDOS(Distributed denial of service)

It is a type of cyber attack where multiple systems are used for DOS. 

 

The machines used in DDOS attack are called botnets

 Example: UDP flood attack, SYN flood attack, fragment packet attacks, ping for death etc..,

topics.title: SYN flood attack
topics.content:
SYN flood attack is a DoS/DDoS attack that abuses TCP’s 3-way handshake by sending many SYN (connection request) packets but never completing the handshake.

 

“SYN sent → Server says OK (SYN-ACK) → But the attacker never says OK back.”

Mitigation:

  • Use anti ddos technology (Arbor)
  • Rate limit.
  • Reduce connection wait time.
  • Deploy load balancers.

topics.title: ARP poisoning or ARP spoofing
topics.content:
ARP Poisoning is a cyber attack where a hacker tricks devices in a network by sending fake ARP messages, making them believe the attacker’s MAC address is the router or another device.

Mitigation:

  • Use static ARP
  • Use XARP tools
  • Set up packet filtering
  • Install AV and keep the signature updated.

topics.title: MITM attack
topics.content:
A MITM attack is when a hacker secretly places themselves between two communicating parties (client and server) to intercept or manipulate traffic without their knowledge.

Same as sniffing but her communication is altered

 

Mitigation: 

  • Use static arp
  • Use encryption
  • Use IPS

topics.title: DNS poisoning / DNS spoofing
topics.content:
DNS Spoofing is a cyber attack used to redirect victims to a malicious or attacker-controlled website by manipulating DNS responses. In this attack, the attacker injects false IP mappings into a DNS server or DNS cache, so legitimate domain requests are resolved to a fake destination. This allows the attacker to impersonate real services, track users, steal credentials, or serve malware while the victim believes they are on the correct website.

Mitigation: 

  • Regularly audit DNS zones.
  • Keeping DNS server up to date
  • Redirect zone transfers
  • Limit recursive queries
  • Store only data only related to the requested domain.

topics.title: What is Malware?
topics.content:
Malware is malicious software designed to intentionally damage, disrupt, or gain unauthorized access to systems or data. 

Attackers deploy it for goals like data theft, financial gain, surveillance, or system disruption. Malware spreads through methods such as phishing, infected files, USB drives, vulnerable services, or network propagation, and preventing it requires layered security, user awareness, and system hardening.

 

Virus:  it attaches itself to the clean files and infect other clean files. Their intention is to damage the system’s core functionalities and delete or corrupt files.

 

Trojan: is a type of malware, which seems to be a legitimate file but contains malicious intent.

 

Worms: are a type of self replicating malware, once it's infected any device it can move through  the network and can compromise the whole network.

Spyware: spyware is malware designed to spy on you. It hides in the background and takes notes activities like surfing habits, passwords, credit card details etc..,

Ransomware: this kind of malware typically locks down your computer and files, and threatens to erase everything unless you pay a ransome.

Adware: though not always malicious in nature. Aggressive advertising software can undermine the security just to serve ads. In turn it can give access to other malware easy ways in, all these activities consume system resources.

Botnets:  Botnets are networks of infected computers that are made to work together under the control of an attacker.

RAT (remote access trojan): type of malware that allows an attacker to gain unauthorized remote access to the victim's machine.

topics.title: Drive by download
topics.content:
Drive-by Download is an attack where malware is automatically downloaded to your device just by visiting a compromised or malicious website, without needing to click anything.

It exploits browser, plugin, or software vulnerabilities to silently install harmful files or scripts.

 

Mitigation:

  • Encourage users to keep their software updated
  • Install antivirus
  • Install web-filttering software
  • Restrict add-ons on browsers
  • Educate users not to visit untrusted websites.

topics.title: SQL injection
topics.content:
SQL Injection is a code injection attack that exploits unsanitized user inputs, allowing attackers to inject malicious SQL statements. This can compromise database confidentiality and integrity by enabling unauthorized access, data manipulation, or deletion.”

Mitigation

  • Input validation.
  • Sanitize all inputs.
  • Use IPS and WAF solutions.
  • Avoid database errors on production applications.

topics.title: Broken authentication

Broken Authentication is a vulnerability caused by weak identity management, insecure login mechanisms, or unsafe session handling. It allows attackers to compromise accounts, impersonate users, or gain unauthorized access to systems.

Mitigations:

  • Rate Limiting & Account Lockouts

topics.title: Splunk architecture
topics.content:
SLUNK ES (enterprise security): is SIEM solutions, which contains the main components

 

  1. Forwarder
  2. Indexer

Forwarder: it is an agent which will be installed on all the log sources from where we need to fetch the logs. Mainly two types of forwarder

  1. Universal forwarder
  2. Heavy forwarder

Universal forwarder: it will forward raw data without doing prior treatment like indexing and normalising.

Heavy forwarder:  it will perform the parsing and indexing at the source before sending the logs to the indexer.

 

Indexer: it acts as a directory where it will store the data based on the source time and time of the log.

Four types of indexers which are generally called buckets, where the logs will be stored based on the freshness of the logs. From hot bucket to warm bucket to cold bucket to frozen bucket.

 

 

Where the frozen bucket logs can not be accessed from the search head.

Search head: it provides UI to fetch the logs from different indexer for the purpose of analysis by using SPL(splunk processing language).

topics.title: IBM Qradar architecture
topics.content:
The q-radar architecture mainly has 5 components.

  1. Event collector
  2. Event processor
  3. Console
  4. Flow collector
  5. Floe processor

Event collector: it collects the logs or events from different log sources.

License throttle: it will check the EPF limit and allow the permitted logs.

EPS: no of events SIEM can process per second

DSM (device support module):it is nothing but parsing.

Parsing: conversion of all the raw logs from unstructured to structured format

Categorization: according to the parsed logs it will categorise the data automatically.

Coalescing: it will combine the multiple logs into one single record in order to save the memory.

 

Event processing: it collects the log from event collector and it mainly consist of CRE and aerial DB

 CRE: custom rule engine.

Is nothing but as correlation it contains a set of rules and if any of the rules matches with received logs, it will trigger a correlated event which becomes an offence(same alert in splunk).

 

Ariel DB: it is database of IBM Q-Radar

 

Console:- it acts as a manager.

  • One copy of data is stored in a real time view or console. Which it collects from CRE.
  • Console consists configuration dashboard, report, searching tabs and offense management
  • By using AQL(aerial query language) we can fetch the required logs.
  • Offensive management receives the correlated events that are called as offenses or alerts.
  • Only the console part connects with the web UI.

Flow collector:  it will collect the flows from different network devices.

Flow processor: contains the information like number of packers sent and received, number of bytes sent and received, it also stores the connection time interval.

topics.title: Malware analysis
topics.content:
Malware analysis is conducted in two ways

  1. Static malware analysis
  2. Dynamic malware analysis.

 

Static: in analysis, analysis will be performed without executing the file.

 

Dynamic:  file will be executed in a secured environment and all the attributes like child process, out bound connections, DNS activity will be analysed to make the decision on the detected files.

Dynamic analysis provide greater detailing on complete analysis of the detected files which includes overview of the file related to size, extension, signature, detection details, Mittre Att&ck mapping, parent princess and child process details, command line, if any registry changes happened, network events connecting to domain, IP address and other IOC’s associated with the file.

topics.title: Short lived account detected
topics.content:
Description: The alert triggers when any username created and deleted within a short period of time, technically which is 5 minutes. Which will be detected using event ID 4720 followed by event ID 4726

 

Log source: Windows event logs, Active directory logs.

 

Gathering information: date and time, source user and user, source IP, host name.

 

Analysis:  we will start with validating the source user detail who performed the creation and deletion of the account by correlating the source IP and source user by using username look up dashboard and hostname look up dashboard.

 

  • If we observe the source user belongs to the active directory(AD) or IAM team, where both have authorization for creating the account. 
  • I will do further analysis with validation by co-relating with other log source like checking the supportive ticket for deleted account or checking the outlook for any prior notifications. Then we will reach out to the user over Microsoft teams to get the business justification of the activity.
  • Based on the source user response we mention the analysis detail in a closure comment and we close the alert as false positive.
  • Technically our client has this use case as a part of validation alert.
  • As part auditing of the alert i observe one of the alerts which is closed as false positive where the source user belongs to the active directory team but the user does not have authorization to create the account but the alert is closed as false positive by mentioning the closure comment which says that user belongs to active directory.
  • Here the analyst did not carry out the further analysis step like, reaching out to the user or creating the supportive ticket.
  • Then I reopen the ticket added to the active directory admin and our manager in the same ticket to inform about the misconfiguration with the authorization to create the account.
  • A further active directory team changed the configuration to reduce the authorized account creation activity.
  • I prepared the report on this incident and presented it during the weekly team meeting for which I got appreciation from our manager.

topics.title: New user added to admin group.
topics.content:
Description: the alert triggers when any user created which can be identified with the help of event ID 4720 and if the same user added to admin group which can be identified with event ID 4732

 

Log source: active directory logs, windows event logs.

 

Gathering information: source user details, account details, source IP and host name.

 

Analysis:  The alert is configured based on the Mittre Attack persistence, which means the attacker might have created the account and added to the privilege or admin group to have greater access so that the attacker can perform CRUD.

 

  •  We will check the source IP used in the activity to make sure whether it is performed by using public IP or Private IP.
  • We need to verify the host involved in the activity whether the host involved in the activity is a managed or unmanaged device. then we will verify the source user who performed the creation and adding of the user to the admin group. Whether the function of the source user is authorised to perform the activity.
  • We will look for any supportive ticket or emails for the user for which account has been created and added to the admin group.
  • Once we will verify all attributes we will take further actions.

Example:

  1. If the internal IP is detected as a source and managed device involved in the activity, the source user is authorized to perform the activity.
  2. If we have a supportive ticket related to a new employee joining the organisation we can close the alert as benign by mentioning the reference ticket number and adding the detailed closure comment carried during the analysis.

topics.title: user reported phishing email.
topics.content:
Description: the alert triggers when more than 3 users reported any email as phishing mail within six hours.

 

 Log source: ESA => Microsoft 365 defender

 

Gathering Info: sender domain, sender mail, address, source IP, subject and receiver details.

 

Analysis:  once the alert triggers o n the incident review dashboard when reported by more than 3 users, we will start validating the reputation of sender domain and associated IP address. By using offline analysis method which include checking the reputation OS INT too;s like virus total, abuse IPDB, IPVoid, MXTools box

  • In our organization we use MS 365 defender as ESA through which we will perform complete email analysis.
  • Once we log in to defender, under email and collaboration in explorer we can filter out the reported mail by using subject line, sender mail address and sender domain.
  • Once we filter out the detected email, we open the email in a new tab to perform complete analysis.
  • In analysis we will validate the sender and recipient details followed by checking the return path and return path domain to validate whether the email is spoofed or not
  • Then we will validate the email authenticate, SPF, DKIM and DMARC.

SPF:  sender policy framework which helps to authenticate whether the mail came from an authenticated user or not by comparing the domain name to IP address.

DKIM: domain key identifying mail which helps to validate the integrity of the mail to make sure the mail is not tampered while following through the different mail server by checking the cryptographic signatures.

DMARC: Domain based message authentication reporting conformance which is the combination of SPF and DKIM.

  • In the meantime we will perform header analysis using Microsoft message header analysis. Apart from this we will also validate related entities like attachment and URLs.
  • Once we click the detected attachment, the defender will give the analysis details and we can also perform the offline analysis by capturing the hash value of the detected file. In the same way we will change the URL in the detected email.

Action and recommendation:

  1. If any negative attributes are observed with respect to the analysis like negative email authentication, negative domain and IP reputation, negative attachment and URL detected we create the incident to purge the email from all the users in_boxes to the ESA team.
  2. We also recommend a proxy and firewall team to block the domain and IP respectively.

Scenario:  if any user found to clicked on any URL that can be identified in URL clicks

 

Then we will check the user activity with respect to login activity to make sure user credentials has not been shared and also we will write the email to user to reset the password

 

If any attachment has been downloaded by the user, we will recommend the EDR team or will create a scan to check the disposition of the file.

 

If any user clicked the url(phishing URL)

If it is malicious to ensure there are any other users clicked on the same URL by going into advanced hunting in defender there we will write the query by referring the URL click events and run it for detected URL. which will give number of users who clicked on the URL so that we can add all the other users to reset the credentials and revolve all active sessions and create the scan on the host to ensure no malicious files were downloaded.

topics.title: Potential malicious URL clicked detection
topics.content:
Description: The alert triggers when any user clicks on the URL which is flagged as malicious by O365(Office 365)

 

Log source: Microsoft 365 defender.

 

Gathering Info: host name, user details, source IP, URl details and action.

 

Analysis: 

  1. The analysis starts from checking the URL details while logging into the defender where we can find the email which delivered the malicious URL.
  2. Then we will perform the basic header analysis which includes checking sender and recipient details, delivery action, original location, latest delivery location, associated IP address and email authenticates value like, SPF, DKM and DMARC.
  3. Then we will check the reputation of the URL using the OSINT tools like Virus total.
  4. Then by using the sandbox environment KASM tool we will try to check what the URL belongs to.
  5. Before that we will download the original email using O365 to  understand what the email content looks like.
  6. While working on one of the alerts we absorb that URL directing to download a PDF file where the same PDF file is sent as an attachment in the email also.
  7. To verify the attachment. We downloaded the file from the KASM environment and submitted the file into the TRELLICS sandbox to get the detailed file analysis report.
  8. In this particular alert the URL is clean but the PDF file also contains an URL which is taking the user to a phishing site hence we confirm the detection as true positive.
  9. As a part of recommendation we need to verify if any other users are delivered the same email.
  10. By using advanced hunting as a defender. We observe three other users who get delivered with the same email and only that detected user clicked on the URL.
  11. As a precautionary measures we created the ticket to reset the user credential and revoke the running session 
  12. Then we created another ticket to the network team to block the IP in the firewall, URL in proxy and ESA team to purge the email from all the user inboxes.

topics.title: An IP address matched a crowdstrike intelligence indicator that has previously been used in targeted attack.
topics.content:
Description : the alert triggers when internal host communications with the malicious IP address which is stored in the database of the Falcon.

 

Log source: EDR.

 

 Gather information:  hostname, src IP, user details, user agent.

 

 Analysis:  

  1. analysis starts from checking the reputation of detected IP by using OSINT tools like virustotal, IPvoid and AbuseIPDB
  2. Then by going into endpoint detection in falcon, we try to understand the triggering condition.
  3. Then we will look into the command line associated with the detection which helps to identify the user agent associated with the detection.
  4. Then we need to go into host investigation to identify the root cause of the connections
  5. We will export the DNS request in the last CSV format for last 24 hours to match the timeline of the connection.
  6. Once we match with the timeline of DNS request, we observe that the user was accessing some construction website, which redirected to a malicious domain which is assigned detection.
  7. To verify that we open the URL in @KASM which can not be accessed at the time, then we try to access the construction website and do the inspection on the browser which confirmed that from the construction URL user redirected to detection drafts observing the alert.
  8. To ensure any downloads or connections we further try to connect to the host in EDR
  9. To check the download folder we run the command cd/users/hostname/downloads
  10. Then by using ls(list) command we can get the list of downloads in the host.
  11. Since the detected URL can not be accessed no downloads drops are observed.
  12. As a part of remediation, since malicious URL has been accessed we created the ticket to reset the browser and also created one more ticket for blocking URL in proxy and IP in firewall
  13. At the end we also send security communication to user about secure device usage policy.

Updated on 24-12-2025

  1. In crowdstrike EDR to identify where the file got downloaded we can use the event search in investigation there we can search using the file name which will give the events related to the file.
  2. From the events we can search for the event's simple name which is motwWitten which will give the details about the route of the file from where it entered the system which contains the information like host URL and referral URL.

topics.title: O365(office 365) MFA phone removed.
topics.content:
Description:  This rule O365 MFA phone removed is triggered when a change in MFA configuration is detected.

 

Log source: O365 logs, active directory.

 

Gathering information:  Target username, target user email ID, Timestamp, result of action.

 

Analysis:  By using the targeted user email address, I log into Microsoft Azure Entra ID which we use as our active directory, I will check in the overview and in properties section to verify any mobile number is listed in the user details.

  1. I will goto auditlog of the user in the relevant time frame. ill look for the activity type “admin detected security info”. Here I will investigate the details like timestamp, status reason (admin deleted phone method for user) initiated actor and IP address.
  2. I'll analyse the reputation of the IP address using OSINT tools.
  3. I will check the details of the initiated actor in Azure Entra ID whether he is a privileged account holder or not and send him a mail to verify the activity and request for the business justification and also confirm if any supportive ticket is involved in the change.
  4. If the initiator confirms the activity that they updated the phone number or device of MFA authentication and obtained the manager approval, and requests the admin to update the new number for authentication then we close this alert as benign.
  5. If the actor is unresponsive or if the IP is malicious then will escalate this to the IT team to disable the account to prevent further unauthorised access.
  6. Investigate users account activity for any suspicious action that may have occurred during the period when MFA was disabled.
  7. If the user’s email address was changed, reset the email address to the original value and also investigate the reason for the change and ensure it was authorised.

topics.title: attempt to download a malicious file from CLI (command Line Interface)
topics.content:
Description: the alert triggers when any host tries to download the files using the CIRL command.

 

Log source: EDR ->crowdstrike falcon.

 

Gathering information: host name, user details, domain, URL or IP address.

 

 

Analysis: as part of analysis we logged into crowdstrike falcon thereby using the hostname we will filter out the detection.

  1. Once we go into full detection details. We can get the complete details about the alert.
  2. The detection IOA is tagged as CURLGETMalware download.
  3. Then we look into command line associated with the trigger where we identify as github-related URL accessed from the user host
  4. The URL from github trying to download a file where the naming is identified as minor which ensures that the user tried to download the coin miner file from github.
  5. As we went into the process table we identified that the command executed by the node process which runs the CURL command.
  6. As the URL pointing towards the crypto miner setup file the technique involves an attempt to download & execution of the malicious file.
  7. The crowdstrike has killed the process to prevent the script from execution.
  8. As the action clearly attempted to crypto miner on the server indicates possible compromise of the application service or user account running on the server.
  9. As a precautionary measure we network contained the host from the EDR and created a scan on the host.
  10. We escalated the case to the client then involved in a bridge call with our client, the principal analyst POC from the client and SOC team.
  11. In the bridge call analysis we identified that the suspected server contains a vulnerability which is pre-authentication remote code execution as the component version is older.
  12. Since the vulnerability related to pre-authenticated RCE(Remote code execution) we observed http requests from the server. Hence, the user account involved in the activity is also requested to disable.

topics.title: public hosted zone created
topics.content:
Description: the alert triggers when any route 53 zone was created and selected as a public.

 

Log source: AWS

 

Mittre tactic: initial access

 

Gathering info: user details, src IP, Host name and domain name.

 

 

Analysis: as the alert related to the cloud environment the alert will be triggered based on the signals. Which in this case is the creation of a public zone.

 

  1.  I will try to validate the access chain related to the activity where we need to verify the user details, user details, time, the activity, IP address related to the activity, geolocation and user agent.
  2. Once we verify the role of the user, we will verify the events or activity related to create, update, delete, read.
  3. Continuing to that we will verify the success, failed and unauthorized events related to CRUD.
  4. Then we will reach out to the user to get to know about the awareness and business justification for the activity.
  5. As per the role suggestion we need confirmation from the user as the hosted zone is in public which may be caused due to the misconfiguration which may lead to unauthorized exploitation.

topics.title: Azure AD suspicious sign-on
topics.content:
Description:  the alert triggers when an user signin to an account in unusual or risky way.

 

 

Log source: Active directory microsoft azure Entra ID.

 

Gathering information:  user account, location, host involved, time of sign in, sign in location, device used, application accessed, sign in status(failed or successful).

 

 

Analysis:  ill login to the active directory using the user account, i will check on the overview and in the property section will investigate the details of the user like, his designation, department, when was the password changed absorbed, base location and his manager.

 

  1. Now I'll start analysing sing-in logs of the user by matching the time provided in the alert. I'll check the reputation of the IP address by using an offline analysis method and also try to find if it belongs to any VPN.
  2. I'll compare the login location with the user's usual work location to see if it matches.
  3. I'll investigate the device used by the user(mobile or laptop) and browser used during the login and check if it is a registered device (managed device) or not.
  4. Ill check the sign in status to see if was successful or interested or failure and note the reason if the was failure
  5. Ill check if MFA was completed and if any conditional access policies were applied
  6. If we find anything unusual for the user like new IP, location, or unregistered device or MFA was not completed, ill email to user’s manager to confirm the activity and also suggest them to use the different mode of communication other than mail, will create a ticket with all the information during by investigation and attaching proof of evidence collected.
  7. If I receive confirmation from the manager that the user performing the activity will close the alert as false positive.
  8. If we can't validate the sign-in activity with in 24 hours or if the user denies the activity, ill treat the login as suspicious, we will revoke all the active sessions, reset the user's password and send the mail to IT team to assist the user in account recovery and also notify the users manager. Now I will close the alert as a true positive.
  9. If i observe any negative attributes such as malicious IP address, usage of VPN from country of concern, multiple MFA failures, multiple failed login attempt, sign in from multiple countries with in short period of time, ill treat it as malicious activity and immediately I will revoke all the session and reset the user’s password and inform the helpdesk team to assist the user account recovery.

topics.title: Access from unusual user agent(browser)
topics.content:
Description: the alert triggers when any user tries to access an internal resource by using undefined user agent(browser).

 

Log source:  Proxy

 

Gathering info: source IP, host detail, user detail, destination url, http response code, HTTP method, action, bytes sent and bytes received, user agent details.

 

Analysis: since the alert triggered for an unusual user agent, we start with validating the IP involved in the activity to verify if it is private IP or Private IP.

  1. We need to check the user agent involved in the activity whether it is permitted or not. Eg: in our client environment the unmanaged devices are allowed to connect to authorization by using secured browser called
  2. Then we will check when the user joined the organization by using the username look-up dashboard.
  3. If the user found to be joined recently. We will raise the request by creating a ticket to the manager of the detected user to request access for the dedicated browser to communicate with the organisation.
  4. On other case if external IP detected in the alert first we need to validate the IP reputation and geolocation details by using OSINT tools like virus total, abuse IPDB and IP void
  5. If the detected IP found to be malicious or location belongs to out of the business core of our client we recommend to block the IP in all segments of the firewall.
  6. Sometimes we detect the VPN segment IP but users are using the unauthorised user agent. We write the event to the user by providing all the default user agents to the talon browser by providing steps to change the process.

topics.title: Multiple requests to DGA (Domain generative algorithm) domain indicating infection.
topics.content:
DGA: it's a program used by malware to generate a large number of domain name requests with C2C (command and control).

 

Description : the alert triggers when the internal system tries to connect with multiple domains which may look like related to IP loop-up service(DNS Server).

 

Log source:  Proxy and NBA (network behaviour analysis) tool alpha SOC

 

Gathering info:  Source IP, hostname, user details, URL, Action.

 

Analysis: the analysis starts from gathering info about user designation and department to ensure it does not belong to the information security department so that we can rule out the alert as benign.

 

  1. Next we need to check the base file, filename. Which created the domain request, to verify that either we can go with searching the log siem, splunk search or by going into the host repository in crowdstrike falcon (EDR).
  2. In crowdstrike falcon we’ll go into host management by using host name we’ll download networking activity related to domain request in CSV format, there we’ll perform defiltering to validate further.
  3. In this particular alert the request created by chrome browser, user trying to access some gaming website but that landed into a different page.
  4. Next we need to check the domain reputation by using OSINT tools and found around 3 engines reported this domain as malicious.
  5. To verify the authenticity of the URL we try to access the URL in KASM where we got the result as 404 not found. We did the same activity for other detected domains which resulted the same.
  6. As per the analysis it is detected that user tries to access some gaming website which landed into untrusted domains and alert got triggered when we check the action taken by the proxy found to be benign
  7. Once we have the root cause as a part of precautionary measure we created the ticket to enterprise security admin team to reset the chrome browser and also created one more ticket to block the malicious domain detected in the alert and also informed the user about the device usage policy like not to connect to untrusted domain using managed devices, we close this alert as true positive

topics.title: multiple file transfer to external domain.
topics.content:
Description: the alert triggers when any internal user transfers the file to external domain which is detected by MS PURVIEW DLP POLICY

 

Log source: MSPURVIEWDLP(Data loss prevention).

 

Gathering information: user details, destination domain details, file details.

 

Analysis: since it is a DLP alert we work on these alerts when escalated by the external DLP support team.

 

  1.  Once we get the escalation we will start looking into notes provided in the escalation. In one of the alerts we observed that the user was uploading the file to an AI website.
  2. Then we start looking into detected files by the DLP policy which will be provided by the DLP support team in the form of CSV.
  3. We will go and verify the files to identify by the file name to make a decision on the security of the content.
  4. Sometimes it is difficult to make decisions based on the filename then we will drop the security notification to the user's manager to validate the file sensitivity.
  5. While having the conversation with the user we get to know that the user didn't upload the files to the AI domain, but the user is using one of the AI extensions which uploaded the files to another domain.
  6. With this observation we created the ticket and also looped our internal trusted AI team to define the policies related to using AI within the organisation environment.

topics.title: process triggered for a high severity custom rule.
topics.content:
Description:  we have some custom IOA rules configured in crowdstrike EDR for some domains, files and IP addresses. Whenever any alert matches the custom IOA detection, the alert will trigger.

 

Log source: EDR => crowdstrike falcon.

 

Gathering information: user details, host details.

 

Analysis: whenever the custom IOA detection happens, we will go into crowdstrike EDR endpoint detection to find the detection details using the host name.

 

  1.  As we have different types of IOAs first we need to understand the custom IOA rule configured for this detection.
  2. If the detected IOA is related to the domain, we will go into host selection or module in falcon in the networking tab. We can get to see all the domain activity associated with the host.
  3. We will export the csv file to carry out the further analysis to verify if the IOA rule listed domain exists or not.
  4. We will try to check DNS events just before the detection to verify if it is redirected from any other url.
  5. To double check the redirection we will run the URL in the KASM secured environment then inspect on the page to check the networking activity of the URL.
  6. Then we will check the base filename which created the DNS activity in the event search of the falcon.
  7. As part of remediation activity we will create the request for browser reset if URL connected by the browser like chrome or edge
  8. After checking, if no downloads are observed in the command line we will write the user about device usage policy and also we will create a networking ticket to block the URL into the proxy.
